title: Work Attire Guidelines
text:
At It Company, our dress code is based on the principle of "Dress for the Occasion." Employees are expected to adjust their attire each day based on their work environment, scheduled meetings, and the activities of the day.
- Client Meetings: When meeting with clients, whether at their location, virtually, or at our offices, employees should always dress in a way that meets or exceeds the client's expectations. This generally means more traditional business attire such as business suits, sport coats/blazers, dress shirts/tops, slacks/skirts, ties, and dress shoes.
- Office Environment: For employees working in the office under normal business conditions, attire should be professional but can be more casual. Below are general guidelines for appropriate office attire:
Appropriate Attire:
- Jeans (without holes, rips, or tears)
- Polo shirts
- Button-up shirts/tops
- Blouses and shells
- Sweaters and vests
- Company logo wear
- Business-appropriate dresses or skirts (of appropriate length)
- Dress sandals
- Casual shoes, including clean athletic shoes
Inappropriate Attire:
- Shorts
- Hats or beanies
- Crop tops or graphic t-shirts
- Flip-flops
- Halter tops or tank tops
- Athletic or workout clothing
- Clothing that is ripped, frayed, or stained
If you are ever uncertain whether your attire is appropriate, we recommend using good judgment and opting for more formal attire when in doubt.
Reasonable Accommodations: It Company is committed to considering reasonable accommodations to our Work Attire Guidelines for medical and/or religious reasons. Please contact Human Resources for more information or if you wish to request an accommodation.
For any questions or clarifications about this policy, please reach out to Human Resources.
